newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon says not attending Cairo economic summit.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says not attending Cairo economic summit.

text.p: Lebanon said it would not attend next month's economic summit in Cairo aimed at integrating Israel into the regional economy, arguing such meetings were premature and futile before full Arab-Israeli peace.

Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri told Paris-based Orient Radio on Saturday "things will be normal" between Israel and its Arab neigbours only after full peace between them, based on an Israeli withdrawal from all occupied Arab land.
"Before that happens, it is like placing the cart before the horse," he said in the interview that was published by Beirut newspapers on Sunday.
"Lebanon, though it was invited, did not attend the first conference in Morocco, nor the second confernce in Amman. Of course, we will not attend the third meeting to be held in Cairo," Hariri said.
"The reason for our position is that this matter is (taking place) prematurely on the one hand, and on the other, we think this method will not lead to any results," he added.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has warned Israel it may be be pressured by Arab countries at the November 12-14 conference, which will group 85 states and some 25 international groups, unless it makes progress in peace talks with the Palestinians.

Hariri said the only way for peace in the Middle East was an Israeli pullout from all occupied Arab land, particularly the Golan Heights occupied from Syria after the 1967 Middle East war and south Lebanon where Israel occupies a border zone.

"There is no other way. All other ways have been tried during the past 20 or 30 years," added Hariri, who on Friday urged President Bill Clinton in talks at the White House to help jump start the stalled peace talks.
Hariri reiterated Lebanon's stand that it will continue to go hand-in-hand with Syria in their peace talks with Israel. Syria is Lebanon's main power broker with 35,000 troops there.
